prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- Pick the platform that fits your priorities. If you want a wide variety of unique homes and experiences, Airbnb. If you want whole vacation homes aimed at families/groups, Vrbo. If you want hotel-like instant booking, lots of properties with flexible payment/cancellation options, or last-minute availability, Booking.com.  
- Always book and pay through the platform, read recent reviews, verify host responsiveness, and ask targeted questions before booking.

How the three platforms differ (practical highlights)
- Airbnb
  - Very large, diverse inventory (private rooms, shared stays, unique/“experience” listings).
  - Clear host profiles, Superhost program, ID verification and guest/host messaging.
  - Service and cleaning fees can be high; cancellation policies vary by host.
  - Good for unique stays, solo travelers, couples, experiential travel.
- Vrbo
  - Focus on whole-homes and family/group rentals (fewer private-room options).
  - Owned-listings (more owner-to-guest relationships) and strong family-focused filters.
  - Fees similar to Airbnb in many cases; owner-managed bookings more common.
  - Good for family vacations, multi-bedroom houses, condos.
- Booking.com
  - Mix of hotels, apartments, and vacation rentals; heavy emphasis on instant booking and last-minute options.
  - Many listings offer free cancellation and pay-at-property choices.
  - Often better for travelers who prefer hotel-like booking flow and immediate confirmations.
  - Good for flexible plans, business travel, or if you want hotel alternatives with easy cancellation.

How to find a good host — checklist
1. Reviews
   - Read recent reviews (last 12 months) for the most relevant info.
   - Look for multiple reviewers praising communication, cleanliness, accuracy of listing, and local tips.
   - Watch for repeated complaints (cleanliness, noisy neighbors, misleading photos).
2. Host profile & verification
   - Prefer hosts with a profile photo, verified ID, and a history of stays.
   - Look for Superhost/Top-Rated/Verified badges (platform-specific).
   - Check how long the host has been on the platform and total number of reviews.
3. Responsiveness
   - Use the platform messaging to ask questions before booking; note response time and clarity.
   - Fast, helpful answers are a good sign.
4. Listing accuracy
   - Check that photos match the description and that sleeping arrangements / bed counts are explicit.
   - Confirm exact address or at least neighborhood. Don’t assume proximity to attractions without checking.
5. House rules & extra fees
   - Confirm cleaning fees, security deposits, additional guest charges, and strictness of house rules (noise, check-in/out).
6. Verification from other sources
   - Cross-check the property on multiple platforms for consistent photos and calendar; inconsistent listings can be a red flag.

Red flags to avoid
- Host asks to pay outside the platform (wire transfer, Venmo, cash). Never do this.
- No reviews and a very low price compared to similar listings.
- Host demands unusually detailed personal info not needed for a stay.
- Vague or evasive answers about check-in, parking, or neighborhood safety.
- Inconsistent photos, blurry photos, or stock imagery instead of real pictures.

Questions to ask a host before booking (short message template)
Hi [host name], I’m [first name]. I’m planning to stay with [number] guests from [check-in date] to [check-out date]. A few quick questions:
- Is the bed/room setup as shown in the listing? Any sofa beds or air mattresses?
- What’s your check-in process and exact arrival instructions?
- Where can we park? Is parking included?
- Any building rules or neighborhood noise to be aware of?
- Are towels, linens, and toiletries included? Is there a washer/dryer?
- Are there any additional fees or house rules not in the listing?
Thanks — we’d love to stay if all looks good.

What to do immediately after booking and on arrival
- Confirm check-in details and access code/entry instructions.
- Save the listing address, host contact info, and platform support number.
- On arrival: do a quick walkthrough, take photos of any pre-existing damage, note cleanliness issues, and message the host right away if something is wrong (with photos).
- If the host doesn’t respond and the issue is serious, contact platform support and keep a record of all messages.

Payment & protection
- Always pay on the platform. That gives you documented receipts and platform dispute resolution.
- Read the cancellation policy carefully before booking. Consider travel insurance if your trip is non-refundable or expensive.
- For extra peace of mind, check the platform’s guest refund policy and any COVID-related flexibility if still relevant.

Negotiation and saving tips
- For longer stays or off-season dates, message the host politely and ask if a discount is possible.
- Filter by “instant book” if you want fast confirmation or by flexible cancellation if plans may change.
- Compare total price (including cleaning and service fees) across platforms — the same property can appear with different totals.

Quick decision guide
- Pick Airbnb if you want unique stays or local experiences and a big selection.
- Pick Vrbo for whole-home rentals for families/groups.
- Pick Booking.com if you prioritize instant booking, hotel-like options, or flexible cancellation/pay-at-property.

If you want, tell me:
- destination, travel dates, party size, and priorities (price, cleanliness, location, cancellation flexibility), and I’ll suggest which platform and what to look for in specific listings — or draft a tailored message to send to hosts.
